claims.text: Large language models encode parametric knowledge about world facts.
Large language models show remarkable performance in knowledge-driven NLP tasks.
Reliance on parametric knowledge may cause large language models to overlook contextual cues.
Overlooking contextual cues leads to incorrect predictions in context-sensitive NLP tasks.
Contextual faithfulness in large language models can be significantly improved using carefully designed prompting strategies.
Opinion-based prompts and counterfactual demonstrations are the most effective prompting strategies for enhancing faithfulness.
Neither opinion-based prompts nor counterfactual demonstrations require additional training.

evidence.description: Experiments on three datasets across machine reading comprehension and relation extraction demonstrate significant improvement in contextual faithfulness.

methodologies.name: Opinion-based prompts
methodologies.description: Reframes the context as a narrator's statement and inquires about the narrator's opinions to improve contextual faithfulness.

methodologies.name: Counterfactual demonstrations
methodologies.description: Uses in-context instances containing false facts to improve faithfulness in knowledge conflict situations.

limitations.text: LLMs rely on parametric knowledge which may cause them to overlook contextual cues and make incorrect predictions in context-sensitive tasks.
